title: Authentication and Session Lifecycle
readerIntent: Understand login, tokens, browser restoration, revocation, and internal credentials.
owner: Profile login/session services and nAuth credential contracts
summary: Human login issues human tokens; service identity issues internal tokens; refresh rotation and security stamps invalidate sessions without storing usable credentials in clients, logs, or audit.

sections.heading: Human authentication
items: Employee and customer username/password routes are pre-authentication routes but still resolve enterprise and tenant context.
Access tokens are short-lived and audience-bound; target authorization always follows.
Browser restoration keeps refresh credentials in scoped HttpOnly cookies, requires exact Origin and CSRF proof, atomically consumes refresh state, and rotates credentials.
Logout revokes refresh state and expires cookies; lock screen does not silently weaken server session policy.

sections.heading: Internal authentication
items: Service principals own API keys stored as keyed digests.
Internal service tokens are tenant-aware, permissioned, bounded, and issued through the service-token contract.
Service-only routes declare authTokenTypes and reject human tokens even when permissions overlap.
Cron and controlled scheduled work use service identity, not employee credentials.

sections.heading: Failure and proof
items: Fail closed on missing secrets, tenant context, distributed atomic refresh state, stamp state, scope, or permission.
Test wrong credentials, inactive/locked principals, replay, concurrent refresh, expiry, revocation, stamp changes, cross-tenant use, service-only rejection, and distributed invalidation.
